Swiggy SDE Intern | Frontend | 2024 batch
I found out through LinkedIn that Swiggy is currently hiring frontend developer interns. I filled out the google form and also reached out to over 10 people who are managers at Swiggy for a referral. After two weeks, I received the link for the Online Assessment.

**Round 1: Online Assessment (120 mins)**
JS Coding Question (Easy): Based on Javascript object.
React question (Medium): Related to API call and pagination
Multiple choice questions: 10-12 questions on CSS

I successfully completed all the questions in approximately 60 minutes. After 4 days, I received a call from HR informing me that I have been shortlisted for the machine coding round.

**Round 2: Machine Coding Round (60 mins)**
In this round, I was asked to build an OTP input system using React.js. The interviewer allowed me to use any code editor I was comfortable with, so I chose VS Code. It took me around 70 minutes to implement the functionality.

To clear this round, ensure that at the end of the interview, your code should be operational with the core functionalities.

**Round 3: PSDS Round ( 60 mins)**
2 Leetcode Easy-Medium questions : Related to Arrays and Map.
Javascript questions: Polyfills, Regex etc.

This round was the easiest for me, as I am proficient in problem-solving and comfortable working with JavaScript.

**Round 4: HM Round (25 mins)** 
Discussion on projects (He asked about how can I build functionality like split-js library as I have used this library in one of my project)

After five days, I called HR for the results, and she informed me that the feedback was not positive.

**Verdict : Rejected**
Every rejection is a Mock interview for the next interview

I am still looking for a job and if your company is hiring for Interns+FTE (2024 batch) please share your LinkedIn, I will share my Resume with you.

**Please upvote if you found it useful.**

I saw on LinkedIn that Swiggy is currently hiring Frontend Interns *(React)*.

## Round 1 : Technical Interview (DSA)

* **Duration:** 60 Minutes

The first technical round consisted of three coding questions.

Although I don't remember the exact problem statements, the interview included two array-based questions followed by a graph problem. The first array question was relatively straightforward and tested basic array manipulation techniques. The second array problem was more involved and required careful handling of edge cases along with an optimized solution.

My TCS Prime Interview Experience
Hi Leetcoders,

I have always wanted to share my on-campus TCS Prime interview experience to help future students. Here’s how my journey unfolded when TCS visited our college in January 2024 for three profiles:

* Ninja (3 LPA)
* Digital (7 LPA)
* Prime (9 LPA)

**Step 1: TCS NQT Exam**
After applying, TCS asked us to upload all necessary documents and issued an admit card for the NQT exam. The test was conducted at a designated center and lasted 3 hours. It consisted of:

* Aptitude Section: English, Mathematics, Reasoning, and more (section-wise with fixed timings).
* Coding Section: Two coding problems, one easy and one medium (90 minutes total).
**Coding Questions in My Test:**
1. Convert a matrix into a lower triangular matrix.
1. Given a long string, convert it into an r * c matrix under specific mathematical  conditions.
I couldn't solve the first question due to panic but managed to complete the second one, which qualified me for the Prime interview. For context:

* Solving the first coding question leads to a Digital interview.
* Solving the second coding question only leads to a Prime interview.
**Step 2: Interview Process (On-Campus)**
After the NQT results, shortlisted candidates were notified of their respective profiles. My interview was scheduled on-campus at 7 AM, starting at 9 AM.

**Round 1: Panel Interview**
The panel included an HR, a technical member, and a manager. My interview lasted around 15 minutes.

**Questions and Topics:**
Introduction: I gave a brief introduction, mentioning my skills like React and Bootstrap.
Technical Questions:
What is React? What are hooks?
What is Bootstrap?
DSA problem: Transpose a matrix.
I provided two solutions (create a new matrix and use swapping), and the manager was satisfied with the second approach.
What is normalization?
Why MongoDB over SQL (based on my project)?
HR Questions:
Preferred work location and time shifts (day/night).
If offered Ninja, would I join?
**Step 3**: Second Interview (Lucknow Office)
A week later, I was informed that candidates shortlisted for Prime needed to re-interview due to the panel offering many Prime selections. Six of us were called to the Lucknow TCS office.

**Round 2: Panel Interview**
This panel was more experienced, and the interview lasted 50-55 minutes.

**Questions and Topic
